title: Modular Geo-Contract SKU & Retention Toggle Pricing Experiment
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Overview:
This ticket experiments with a modular contract SKU model that lets enterprise customers compose geo-privacy options (EU/UK SCC activation, data residency region selection, and retention toggles) as independent add-ons to a base hosting offering. The goal is to surface clearer pricing signals while keeping procurement friction low for customers who need only a subset of controls.

Hypothesis:
If we provide discrete, well-defined contract modules (e.g., 'EU SCCs + EU data-at-rest', 'UK SCCs + UK data routing', '30d retention opt-in with audit logs') and price them transparently as monthly SKU add-ons, more mid-market customers will onboard without full enterprise negotiation and some enterprise customers will self-select modules rather than request bespoke contracts. Expected lift: 15–25% reduction in sales cycle time for geo/privacy requests and a 10% increase in upsell revenue for modular-add customers over 6 months.

Experiment scope and deliverables:
- Define 4 contract modules with legal and security: EU SCC activation, UK Addendum, Subprocessor Attestation (limited list), and Retention Toggle (30d / 90d / custom).
- Create a pricing matrix mapping modules to list price, per-GB surcharge where applicable, and a minimal one-time activation fee for SCCs where legal processing is required.
- Implement a checkout flow prototype for self-serve sign-up that exposes these modules and calculates estimated monthly cost.
- Draft a concise contract exhibit (1–2 pages per module) that can be appended to T&Cs to avoid full contract redlines.
- Instrument telemetry: track module selection rate, time to first API call post-signup, number of sales-assisted conversions, and legal review reopen events.

Success criteria (30/90/180 days):
- 30 days: Functional prototype of pricing matrix + legal exhibits; PM, Legal, and Sales alignment.
- 90 days: At least 3 customers signed via self-serve with modules; sample sales cycle time reduced by >10% for privacy requests; early telemetry shows >30% of privacy-request customers picking a module vs full contract.
- 180 days: Module-driven revenue >= 7% of new ARR from mid-market segment; documented playbook for converting modules to reserved Dedicated/Private deals.

Key trade-offs and questions:
- Pricing: per-GB surcharge vs flat per-month seat charge. Per-GB aligns cost but complicates billing; flat fee is simple but may undercharge heavy-storage customers.
- SCC activation operational cost: Legal and infra work to certify SCC activation per customer will drive activation fees. How to amortize this cost across customers?
- Subprocessors: Maintaining a short, curated subprocessor list vs a fully dynamic disclosure process. Static lists reduce legal friction but may increase operational risk as vendors change.
- Retention toggles: Technical implementation of configurable retention windows must be verifiable in audit logs for compliance — this adds infra work and observability requirements.

Implementation plan & milestones:
- Week 1–2: Draft module definitions and pricing bands; Legal to draft exhibits; Solutions Engineering to validate technical feasibility of retention toggles and regional routing.
- Week 3–4: Build checkout prototype and pricing calculator; Sales playbook draft; update Console UI spec for module visibility and cost breakdown.
- Week 5–8: Pilot with 3 mid-market customers via Sales-assisted flow; collect feedback and iterate exhibits/pricing.
- Week 9–12: Enable self-serve path for selected modules; monitor telemetry and prepare playbook for expansion.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Leah Morgan (owner), Sandeep Rao (assignee)
- Legal: Priya Kapoor (contracts), Miguel Torres (privacy)
- Security: Naomi Ito (security/compliance)
- Engineering: Infra (runtime routing) lead: Daniel Kim; Console owner: Priyanka Shah; Billing: Jorge Alvarez
- Sales/SE: Marcus Chen (lead AE), Maya Patel (Solutions Engineer)

Open tasks / Known blockers:
- Legal needs buy-in on exhibit language for SCC activation and whether auto-activation is possible for standard templates (blocked until 2025-02-20 meeting).
- Billing systems need schema changes to support per-module line-items and activation fees; billability deadline for the pilot is 2025-03-15.
- Security sign-off on retention toggle auditability required before self-serve is enabled.

Notes on customer-facing positioning:
- Messaging should emphasize flexibility: "Pick only the controls you need — pay only for what you use."
- Provide a short rubric to help customers choose modules: compliance need, contract timeline, and expected monthly token/GB usage.
- Include case studies for common pack combinations (e.g., EU SCCs + 90d retention for European SaaS vendors).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Legal redlines from enterprise buyers who still request bespoke clauses. Mitigation: Offer a fast-track sales-assisted conversion path to Dedicated/Private with predictable SLAs.
- Risk: Underpricing heavy-storage/regulatory customers. Mitigation: capped per-GB surcharge and early billing guardrails during pilot.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Legal and Security to finalize module exhibits (by 2025-02-20).
2) Billing & Engineering to scope implementation effort for retention toggles and moduleized line items (by 2025-02-28).
3) Identify 3 pilot customers and prepare SE playbooks (owner: Marcus Chen) — target signings in March.
